newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA steps up violence, kills Basque court guard.
newsitem.headline: ETA steps up violence, kills Basque court guard.

text.p: Basque ETA separatist rebels struck with deadly force for the fourth time in a week in Spain on Monday, killing a policeman with a car bomb.
Basque court guard Modesto Rico Pasarin, 33, died instantly when a bomb attached to the bottom of his car exploded as he drove out of his garage in the northern Spanish city of Bilbao.
The car was enveloped in flames just five metres (yards) from a high school with 2,000 students, none of whom were hurt.
"We were in class as normal," said one of the students. "The explosion broke the classroom windows and when we looked out we saw the car burning. The man was already dead."
Politicians blamed the attack on the ETA -- Basque Homeland and Freedom -- which has killed 800 people in its 29-year drive for independence, four in the past week.
"This could have caused a massacre because it was just a few metres from a school," said Carlos Iturgaiz, spokesman for the regional party of the ruling conservative Popular Party.
The killing brings to four the number of victims ETA has claimed just this week in a sharp escalation of violence.

Last Monday, a Supreme Court judge was gunned down outside his Madrid home hours after a powerful car bomb exploded in the sourthern city of Granada, killing a civilian airbase worker and wounding seven.
The next days, ETA shot and killed a Basque businessman.

"This is the fruit of an irrational escalation of violence," said Inigo Urkullu, spokesman for the Basque Nationalist Party "ETA is attempting to tear down and destroy its own country and turn it into a fiefdom of intolerance, hate and horror."

The Spanish government had feared a surge in separatist violence this year as ETA tried to reassert itself after a string of setbacks in 1996 that saw several top leaders arrested and a key attack foiled.

In a newspaper interview on Sunday, Spain's top strategist in the battle against ETA, Secretary of State for Security Ricardo Marti Fluxa, was pessimistic about chances for peace and predicted more suffering.
Already this year, the rebels have killed six people, more than those assassinated during all of 1996, severely dampening hopes for a negotiated solution to 29 years of violence.

"With each new attack, with each new kidnapping, with each new act of terror and barbarism a solution to the situation that threatens and retricts the development of our people moves further away," said Urkullu.
The assassination on Monday followed another turbulent weekend in the Basque region, with three people seriously wounded and 20 others injured in a clash between police and supporters of ETA.
The demonstration on Saturday in Bilbao was led by Herri Batasuna (HB), the political arm of ETA, to protest at the arrests this month of HB leaders who failed to respond to a Supreme Court summons.
Three more HB leaders are expected to be detained on Monday.
